svg.text: Safer Online Spaces · ML for Good
A Robustness Audit of CLIP-Fusion Classifiers Under Naturalistic and Adversarial Perturbations
Enric Guasch · [[HENRIK: full name]] · EE-559 Deep Learning · EPFL · May 2026

g.text: Image and text are individually benign, hateful together. CLIP fusion handles the
clean case — but content moderation never sees clean inputs.
hate → h@te, character padding, JPEG compression, brightness shifts:
label-preserving for humans, prediction-flipping for detectors.
Imperceptible ℓ∞ pixel perturbations flip any gradient-accessible classifier.
concat( t, v, |t − v|, t ⊙ v ) ∈ ℝ^2048
AdamW · bf16 · batch 128 · 10 ep · 3 seeds · 1 × A100

svg.text: Splits: dev (n=500) · test_seen (n=1000, 49 % pos) · test_unseen (n=2000, 37.5 % pos).
Decision threshold τ tuned on dev only; reused unchanged on test splits.
A single classifier, two threat models, two parallel “audit + defense” loops.

g.text: Audit grid: 57 single-cell + 16 composite cells × 9 recipes × 3 seeds × 3 splits.
Text is the brittle modality. Worst-cell text ΔAUROC on clean baseline: 0.115 / 0.129 / 0.110.
Composites are the worst threat. composite_2text_2image high reaches Δ 0.140 on test_unseen.
Defense: L = BCE(y, p_c) + α · BCE(y, p_p) + β · KL(p_c ‖ p_p), α=1, β=0.5;
with prob p drop the text branch ⇒ head must commit to a usable image representation.
Sweep result: p ∈ [0.15, 0.25] revives the image branch at zero clean-accuracy cost.

svg.text: Pareto front — Clean AUROC × Image-only AUROC (test_unseen, 3-seed mean)
7-point sweep: p ∈ [0.15, 0.25] gives image-branch revival at zero clean-accuracy cost; p = 0.30 is Pareto-dominated.

g.text: Audit [[HENRIK]]: PGD/FGSM at ε ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}/255 on the image branch.
Expected: clean baseline AUROC collapses by ε = 2/255; < 0.55 by ε = 8/255.
Defense [[HENRIK]]: Madry-style adv. training. Inner PGD at ε=[[HENRIK]], K=[[HENRIK]] steps.
Reuses attacks/pgd.py; wraps inner-max into stage1_robust.py.
Stacked recipe [[HENRIK]]: kldrop-p015 + adv-training — does it compose or trade off?
· severities: low / med / high / mixed (per-component sampling)
· mixed ≈ medium on every recipe — realistic-user threat ≈ medium-severity composite

svg.text: Evaluation protocol: AUROC · macro-F1 · ASR · worst-case-across-families. τ tuned on dev, fixed on test.
★ = jointly Pareto-optimal in the (clean, image-only) plane. Bold = best in column.
6 · The defense stops over-flagging benign content

g.text: Per-example disagreement (kldrop-p015 vs kl, test_unseen): n = 131 / 2000.
97 % of those flips are on label = 0 (bootstrap 95 % CI 94 – 99 %).
Image-branch revival cuts FPs on benign memes that mention
a protected group. Hateful-class recall preserved within seed noise.
EE-559: “differentiate harmful hate speech from satire”
⇒ this is literally the false-positive-rate problem.

svg.text: 7 · Take-away — a recipe for a trustworthy classifier

g.text: A multimodal hate-meme classifier becomes trustworthy only when
CLIP fusion + KL-consistency + text-modality dropout p ∈ [0.15, 0.25].
Image-only AUROC 0.628 → 0.668 on test_unseen, zero clean-accuracy cost.
Cuts FPs on benign content (97 % label = 0 flips); recall preserved.
Adversary case [[HENRIK]]: PGD adversarial training closes ε ≥ 2/255
at [[HENRIK: # pp]] clean cost. Stacked: kldrop-p015 + adv-training [[HENRIK]].
Open: composite_2text_2image high (Δ ≈ 0.14) and [[HENRIK: ε ≥ ?]] remain partially open.
Naturalistic defense is essentially free; adversarial defense costs something.
A deployable moderation tool needs both passes.
